newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-FYNES, STROMAN RUN YEAR'S FASTEST TIMES AT NCAA MEET.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-FYNES, STROMAN RUN YEAR'S FASTEST TIMES AT NCAA MEET.

text.p: Olympians Sevatheda Fynes and Obadele Thompson slipped and slid to impressive sprint wins after newcomer LaTarsha Stroman clocked the year's fastest women's 400 meters Saturday at the rain-hit U.S. collegiate championships.
Fynes, from the Bahamas, delivered the year's top women's 100-meter performance of 11.04 seconds, then clocked the second-fastest 200 meters of 1997, 22.61 seconds, on a wet Indiana University track.
Barbadian Thompson won the men's 100 meters in 10.13 seconds and produced the year's second-fastest 200 meters of 20.03 seconds, despite rain and headwinds.
But the biggest surprise of the day came from Stroman, a 21-year-old Louisiana State University student who has lowered her personal best by 1.6 seconds this year with her victory in 50.60 seconds.

"I got out really well," said Stroman, who ran before the rain came. "Then I heard my coach yell, 'Relax!' So I took a deep breath and as soon as I got to the (200-meter mark) I just started digging and gave it all I had.
"It's a wonderful feeling to be the fastest in the world, but who knowns how long it will last," she said. "But, yes, I think I can run faster."
Fynes had hoped to break 11 seconds in the 100 meters, but she admitted she was pleased with her time, a personal best.
"I had sort of a hard time trying to run," she said of the wet surface, "but I can not complain. I had a great day."
Her 200-meter time was second in the world only to the 20.60 seconds she clocked under drier conditions on Friday.
Whether she will compete in the world championships, though, depends on the Bahamian athletics federation.

She has several weeks of schooling left at Michigan State University this summer and may not be able to attend her country's national championships. If she doesn't, she's hoping the Bahamian federation will automatically include her on its team for the world championships in Athens in August.
Jamaican athletes Roxbert Martin and Astia Walker also had fast times on the final day of the championships.
Martin, a student at the University of Oklahoma won the men's 400 meters in 44.77 seconds. Walker, who attends Louisiana State, clocked 12.85 seconds to win the women's 100-meter hurdles.
